subsystems.name: Device initialization & context model
subsystems.why: The whole process today establishes exactly one 'current device' (thread-local cudaSetDevice in RuntimeImpl::initialize) and every kernel/stream/graph inherits it. The dual-GPU design decision (stream-scoped launches vs per-context setDevice; how many CUDA contexts coexist in one process) is made here.
checklist: RuntimeConfig.device_id (single int) -> device list + tp size
ModelEngine::load cudaGetDeviceCount gate (currently >=1) -> >= tp, and the requested ids must exist
Runtime property queries (SM count, mem clock, bus width, PCI bus id) per device
device_health: note_cuda_error/device_lost are process-global; decide fail-fast (recommended: process death on any GPU error, matching current ops) vs isolate
Confirm CUDA 'current device' is thread-local and document which threads may touch which device (server worker thread, HTTP threads doing submit-time memcpy, lmcache sidecar process)

subsystems.name: Paged KV cache
subsystems.why: One flat pool per of {K,V} (plus int8 scale pools, windowed ring tables, per-sequence block tables) on a single device. KV heads must be split across the two devices; everything built on top (paging, prefix sharing, admission, metrics, lmcache) reads those pools.
checklist: k_pool/v_pool layout [slots, blocks, block_size, kv_heads, head_dim] -> per-device pool holding kv_heads/2 each (or by slot, if head split is uneven)
Block tables: one per device pool; logical block numbering shared, physical independent
int8 KV scale pools (k_scale/v_scale) follow the same split
Windowed (SWA) ring slots and d_win_tables per pool
Prefix sharing refcounts are per physical pool (blocks are never shared across devices; a logical prefix = two halves)
Admission: KV capacity = min over pools (a session needs blocks in every pool it touches)
Auto-sizing budget (80% free VRAM in examples; server formula in ModelEngine) becomes a per-device budget
free_kv_blocks / prefix-cache metrics per pool

subsystems.name: Gated-DeltaNet recurrent state
subsystems.why: 48 of 64 Qwen3.8 layers are GDN and carry per-sequence recurrent state (fp32 lin_state + bf16 conv state) allocated at open_session on one device. The state is per value-head, so it splits cleanly across GPUs -- but every snapshot/restore/rollback path must follow.
checklist: lin_state / lin_conv_state allocation in open_session: split by linear_v_heads (24/24 with 48 heads) or by block convention (gdn_qh_block)
All snapshot paths: prefix-cache pinned-host snapshots (~205 MB on 27B), dflash spec save/restore snapshots, packed-decode bf16 compaction
Prefill recurrent-state initialization (conv state zeroing) per device
Verify no cross-head coupling in the GDN update (it must be independent per v-head or the split is invalid)

subsystems.name: MoE router & expert dispatch
subsystems.why: MoEEngine allocates its scratch (router logits, top-k ids, weights, counts) on the current device and all expert weights live on that device. Qwen3.8-27B is dense_ffn (n_experts=1, top_k=1) so it takes the dense special-case; Qwen3.6-35B-A3B would split 256 experts.
checklist: Scratch buffers per MoEEngine instance (one per device)
27B: single 'expert' = one big SwiGLU FFN -> column-split gate/up, row-split down (see layout appendix)
35B-A3B: expert residency split (E/2 per device) incl. expert_cache_slots budget and async_expert_prefetch per device
Router GEMM: input hidden is full on both devices -> replicate the router or run on device 0 and broadcast; counts/dispatch lists are then per device
launch_moe_expert_ffn* kernels: dispatch only this device's experts

subsystems.name: Weight loading & conversion
subsystems.why: Every loader mallocs the complete model into one device (17.9 GB > 16 GB). Loaders must place each tensor per the ownership map, including the opportunistic extra-format copies (o_fp4/down_fp4/wo_fp4/gate_fp4) that are currently gated on one device's free VRAM.
checklist: Per-tensor ownership map (P3 deliverable) consumed by all three loaders (GGUF, compressed-tensors, flat .bin)
GGUF quantized-in-VRAM experts: split by expert index; dequant scratch per device
Free-VRAM preflight gates become per-device decisions (an fp4 copy may fit on one card and not the other)
DSpark drafter placement (replicate vs split) per CHG-0030
Vision tower placement per CHG-0031
runtime/tools/convert_qwen35.py: output layout must support split placement (or prove it doesn't need to)

subsystems.name: Decode hot path (single/packed token)
subsystems.why: The token loop: embed -> 64 layers (16 attention + 48 GDN) -> final norm -> lm_head -> argmax, with 4 forked streams, events, one decode graph per session (parked per session), adaptive n_splits sized from SM count, and a recursive device_mutex that serializes capture against legacy-stream work. All of it is one-context today.
checklist: Streams stream/stream_k/stream_v/stream_pf: per-device sets; cross-device event pairs at all-reduce points
Decode graph capture (cu_graph + per-session parking lot): capture-on-two-contexts rules; P2P memcpy nodes need peer access ENABLED at capture time (R5)
Prefill graph and dflash verify graph: same treatment
adaptive n_splits / split tiers: sized for 170 SM (5090); 48 SM cards need retuned constants (kernel subsystem)
lm_head: row-split by vocab + cross-device argmax (greedy) / Gumbel-max (temperature)
device_mutex semantics with two contexts (the documented capture-poisoning hazard is per-context legacy-stream sync; restate the invariants)
Packed decode (decode_packed, graph tiers up to 32 rows): per-device row handling + all-reduce per layer group

subsystems.name: Batched/chunked prefill
subsystems.why: 5.6k-line batched prefill: fused qkvg grouped GEMM, NVFP4/FP8/Int8 GEMM families, chunked prefill, multi-prompt ingestion, DFlash context buffers. Same tensor split as decode, but GEMMs are row-split and their outputs feed the per-device state; the verify (dflash) pass spans both.
checklist: Fused qkvg operand [2*qdim + 2*kvdim, H]: split rows per q/kv head groups
Grouped/batched GEMM split-K variants: partial sums must recombine with the same numerics decision as decode (R2)
Chunked prefill windows and GDN state continuation across windows, per device
ingest_prompts_packed (multi-session): each session's state on both pools
Prefill graph tiers: per-device or hybrid capture

subsystems.name: ContinuousBatchEngine & sessions
subsystems.why: One worker thread drives the single device; admission tickets count KV blocks from one pool; prefix-cache entries hold recurrent-state snapshots in pinned HOST memory (device-agnostic); the DSpark drafter and the vision tower are extra models with their own residency; the lmcache sidecar is a FORKED process with its own CUDA setup.
checklist: Worker: one thread driving both devices (streams, not setDevice) vs one thread per device -- decide (one thread is simpler; streams make it device-independent)
Admission: capacity = min over the two KV pools; waiting tickets unchanged
open_session/close_session: per-pool block allocation + per-device GDN state
DSpark: drafter residency (CHG-0030); verify pass on both devices; the byte-lossless-vs-AR gate must be re-proven inside tp=2 (R2)
Prefix cache: snapshots become per-device pairs; LRU policy unchanged (host-resident)
Vision tower: run on one device and P2P-broadcast embeddings, or replicate (CHG-0031)
lmcache sidecar: its own device assumptions; likely defer the dual-GPU KV tier to v2 (CHG-0017)

items.change: 2026-09-25 (user decision): NCCL-based. One 2-rank communicator (init outside graph capture, destroy at shutdown); allreduce = ncclAllReduce(bf16) on per-device streams; maxreduce = ncclMax over vocab-split lm_head logits (greedy = cross-device max of local maxima; sampling = Gumbel-max compare). NCCL selects P2P vs SHM host-staging automatically, so G1 is informational (recorded by the WP-1 probe), not a design branch. Fallback (R8): the original hand-rolled design — peer copy + local add, P2P-mapped or pinned-staging, one API, no host sync — behind the identical header: zero rework upstream, original no-deps promise restored.
items.verification: Dedicated tests: 2-GPU all-reduce vs host reference (bf16), NCCL transport forced/observed (NCCL_P2P=0/1), cross-context event ordering, 100x init/teardown leak check, P2P-vs-staged bandwidth report

The original hand-rolled scope (2-GPU ring all-reduce: each device copies its half to the peer, both add; P2P mapped-memory fast path; pinned-host staging fallback) is kept as the recorded fallback if NCCL cannot run on this pair (R8, answered by the WP-1 probe).
